geometry.locator: src:geo-lngs-pee-2024 p.27-28 (chainage); walked along geometry:lngs-tunnel-gran-sasso's own OSM line
geometry.note: The straight-line distance between the two endpoints below (710.0 m by haversine) matches the official chainage delta (124.150 - 123.440 = 0.710 km) to within 4 m, which corroborates that A24 motorway chainage and this OSM way's own cumulative length correspond closely over this stretch (the whole-tunnel length check on geometry:lngs-tunnel-gran-sasso passes at 0.10%). A different part of the same source states the door-to-door distance is 'ca. 500 m' rather than the 710 m implied by its own two km markers; both figures are reported here (see the facility worklog) rather than silently reconciled.

method: Walked along geometry:lngs-tunnel-gran-sasso's line from its Assergi (west) end, cumulatively (haversine, 45 vertices): 5787 m (the laboratory's exit doors) to 6497 m (its entrance doors). The two distances come from the official emergency plan's A24 motorway chainage: the tunnel bore runs km 117.653 (Assergi portal) to km 127.829 (Teramo portal); the laboratory's own doors are stated at km 124.150 (entrance) and km 123.440 (exit); subtracting the portal chainage (117.653 km) from each gives the distance-from-Assergi-portal used here. Both target distances fell on the same original OSM segment, so the drawn line is a straight 2-point sub-segment of the tunnel line, not a freehand shape.
name: LNGS underground laboratory access zone (Gran Sasso tunnel, km 123.440-124.150)
notes: This is the sourced stretch of the highway tunnel adjacent to the laboratory's entrance and exit doors, not a hall footprint: no fetched source this session gives the perpendicular offset, orientation or footprint of Halls A/B/C from the highway tunnel centreline, only their combined dimensions (about 100 x 20 x 18 m each, src:geo-euro-ug-pandola-2011) and this along-tunnel span. See geometry:lngs-hall-a/-b/-c for the (undifferentiated) hall markers derived from this zone's midpoint.

summary.plain: The roughly 700-metre stretch of the Gran Sasso highway tunnel next to the LNGS underground laboratory's own entrance and exit doors, about 6 km in from the Assergi end.
